news.headline: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say
news.story_lead: - Published 9 November 2026, 06:23 GMT A gunman suspected of killing six people in Krakow has died in hospital, Polish police say. The 24-year-old, who ministers said was apparently inspired by "far-right ideologies", was injured after opening fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland, on Saturday. Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said.
news.full_article_text: - Published 9 November 2026, 06:23 GMT A gunman suspected of killing six people in Krakow has died in hospital, Polish police say. The 24-year-old, who ministers said was apparently inspired by "far-right ideologies", was injured after opening fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland, on Saturday. Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said. Krakow police said the suspected gunman died early on Monday morning. After the shooting, which began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's busy Main Market Square, police identified the attacker as a 24-year-old Polish man but did not confirm his name. In the hours after the shooting, a minister has said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details. Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed in the attack. People run for shelter as gunshots heard in Krakow Four victims are Polish, while a British national and an Austrian woman were also killed. Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack. On Sunday, Polish police confirmed those three victims had been identified as the alleged gunman's 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother and his sister, who was 21 years old. Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home. Sixteen people, including five foreigners, two police officers and the attacker, were taken to hospital. The interior ministry later said they were from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia. In the wake of the shooting, Poland declared the country would enter two days of national mourning. After travelling to Krakow, Tusk said: "Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism...that's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow." The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the people of Poland," he added. news.headline: Delhi records 3rd worst Diwali pollution since '21, data gaps cloud full picture
news.story_lead: Delhi records 3rd worst Diwali pollution since '21, data gaps cloud full picture More than half the air quality stations in the national Capital stopped reporting air quality data around midnight. Many of the city’s air quality stations going dark on Diwali night does not help in answering this question consistently. And the warmer night perhaps helped despite firecrackers being used well beyond prescribed limits.
news.full_article_text: Delhi records 3rd worst Diwali pollution since '21, data gaps cloud full picture More than half the air quality stations in the national Capital stopped reporting air quality data around midnight. Many of the city’s air quality stations going dark on Diwali night does not help in answering this question consistently. And the warmer night perhaps helped despite firecrackers being used well beyond prescribed limits. The air, despite relatively favourable weather, is still close to the 'severe category' – the threshold for pollution reaching its most harmful levels. More than half the stations went dark, over 80% functioning in “severe” range A consistent comparison of Diwali air pollution requires comparable data over time. More than half the air quality stations in the national Capital stopped reporting air quality data around midnight. This happened even as the stations that continued to report data found the air “severe” or with the Air Quality Index (AQI) above 400. Around 80% of functioning stations were reporting air in the “severe” range from the hour starting 10pm on Diwali to the hour ending 6am on the morning after. At 9 pm, on Diwali night, the latest reading after which the number of reporting stations fell sharply, 61% of the reporting 57 stations had an AQI of 400 or more. To be sure, AQI is generally calculated by calculating sub-indices for multiple pollutants and choosing the highest sub-index as the AQI. HT has limited itself to the PM2.5 sub-index throughout this analysis to look at the widest range of stations across years. Deep Dive The third worst Diwali night since at least 2021 While data gaps make comparison across years difficult (the stations that go dark are not necessarily the same every year), HT has overcome this problem by looking at six stations that have reported data for most of Diwali’s peak hours in all years since 2021: Alipur, Aya Nagar, Bawana, IHBAS-Dilshad Garden, Narela, and Punjabi Bagh. Going further back reduces the number of stations further. The average of these six stations shows that Delhi’s air has been the third most polluted for most hours since Diwali night. The peak PM2.5 sub-index at these stations averaged 655 – recorded at the hour ending 1am in the early morning after Diwali. The only higher peak pollution – in terms of hourly averages – was recorded in 2021 and 2025, when these values were 812 and 752. The number was much lower in the 2022-2024 period, when the peak was 483,583, and 489. To be sure, there are two hours after the peak – the hour ending 4am and 5am – when pollution this year was the second highest after 2021. However, that is possible because of gaps in data which is available. The stations were selected if they had data for at least 9 hours in the period starting 6pm on Diwali and ending at 6am the morning after. Favourable weather likely helped bring Diwali peak down this year As the previous chart shows, Diwali started off much worse than it ended. Up to the hour starting 7am on November 8, Delhi’s air averaged the worst since 2021. It was the second worst even up to the hour starting 7pm. It is only after that hour that 2026 air is ranked the third most polluted. This can happen in largely two ways: somewhat fewer firecrackers being burst this year or weather turning more favourable. The latter is the more likely answer. Meteorological Aerodrome Report (METAR) data from Palam – collated by Iowa State University – shows that this has been the third to fourth warmest Diwali since 2021 across different hours of Diwali. In some hours, it was also almost as windy as 2022-2024, some of the relatively cleaner Diwali years. This would have helped in clearing some pollutants. In other words, without help from meteorological factors, this could have been an even more polluted morning after Diwali. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Abhishek Jha Abhishek Jha is Assistant Editor-Data at Hindustan Times. He uses statistical programming to generate newsworthy insights from large datasets. He is part of the team that produces Number Theory, a daily data story feature of the paper’s print edition. Since March 2024, he has been writing Weather Bee, a weekly column for the Hindustan Times website. He is a chemical engineer by training, who specialises in stories related to weather, climate, and the environment. Jha has been at HT since 2018, where he offers data-driven perspective and analysis on politics, environment, weather, climate, economy and society. His work includes data coverage of elections in India and abroad, including the 2019 and 2024 Lok Sabha elections; the disasters and extreme weather resulting from changing climate, such as floods, droughts, heat waves, cold waves, and dwindling snow cap in the Himalayas; the factors that drive poor air quality in northern India; the changing patterns of land use; the Covid-19 pandemic and its impact on labour market conditions; the changing pattern of consumer spending seen in the new consumer spending surveys; and social norms seen in the surveys such as the National Family Health Survey. news.headline: Mumbai pollution spikes overnight after Diwali firecrackers, AQI crosses 400 at several spots
news.story_lead: Mumbai pollution spikes overnight after Diwali firecrackers, AQI crosses 400 at several spots Diwali firecrackers triggered overnight pollution spikes in Mumbai, with Navy Nagar recording an AQI of 497 and several areas crossing 400. Firecracker bursting on Diwali night led to a sharp rise in pollution in Mumbai , with nine of the city’s 25 air quality monitoring stations recording poor air quality on Monday morning. news.headline: Kerala Begins Random Ethanol Inspections at Fuel Outlets Following Excess Blending Concerns
news.story_lead: The Kerala state government has initiated surprise ethanol testing at petrol pumps across four districts to ensure compliance with the mandated 20 percent blending cap. The decision follows public complaints of vehicle damage in Kerala and recent claims from Karnataka that fuel containing over 30 percent ethanol was being distributed.
news.full_article_text:
The Kerala government has launched random ethanol testing at fuel retail outlets in four key districts: Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam, Kozhikode, and Kannur. Kerala Food and Civil Supplies Minister Anoop Jacob stated that the inspection drive was ordered to address growing public concerns over vehicle damage attributed to excessive ethanol content in petrol, alongside troubling reports emerging from neighbouring Karnataka.

Under current national standards, ethanol content in petrol must not exceed the permissible limit of 20 percent (E20). Minister Jacob clarified that fuel samples collected randomly by inspection teams will be analyzed at a state government laboratory, with official test results expected within 10 days. Outlets found selling petrol with ethanol levels above 20 percent will be sealed immediately, and criminal prosecution will be initiated against responsible stakeholders.

The enforcement drive relies on statutory powers granted under a 2014 state notification issued pursuant to the Central Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply and Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005. This framework authorizes state officials, ranging from the Commissioner of Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs to Taluk Supply Officers, to conduct inspections, collect samples, and pursue legal action against non-compliant outlets.

The state's crackdown follows allegations raised by Karnataka Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology Minister Rizwan Arshad. Tests conducted on petrol samples collected during October 2026 across seven Karnataka regions—Bengaluru, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Bengaluru Rural, Ramanagara, Mangaluru, and Tumakuru—allegedly revealed ethanol concentrations reaching as high as 31.2 percent. However, public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs) have rejected these findings, maintaining that their E20 fuel strictly adheres to Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) specification IS 17021 and questioning the testing methodology used by Karnataka officials.

hindi_translation.headline: कर्नाटक विवाद के बाद केरल ने ईंधन आउटलेट्स पर एथेनॉल की आकस्मिक जांच शुरू की
hindi_translation.story_lead: केरल सरकार ने तय 20 प्रतिशत सीमा के अनुपालन का पता लगाने के लिए चार जिलों के पेट्रोल पंपों पर एथेनॉल की आकस्मिक जांच शुरू की है। यह कार्रवाई केरल में वाहनों के नुकसान की शिकायतों और कर्नाटक में पेट्रोल में 30 प्रतिशत से अधिक एथेनॉल पाए जाने के दावों के बाद की गई है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
केरल सरकार ने चार प्रमुख जिलों: तिरुवनंतपुरम, एर्नाकुलम, कोझिकोड और कन्नूर के चुनिंदा ईंधन खुदरा आउटलेट्स पर आकस्मिक एथेनॉल परीक्षण शुरू किया है। केरल के खाद्य एवं नागरिक आपूर्ति मंत्री अनूप जैकब ने कहा कि यह निरीक्षण अभियान पेट्रोल में अत्यधिक एथेनॉल के कारण वाहनों के क्षतिग्रस्त होने की जनता की आशंकाओं और पड़ोसी राज्य कर्नाटक से आई रिपोर्टों के बाद शुरू किया गया है।

वर्तमान नियमों के अनुसार, ईंधन में एथेनॉल की अधिकतम अनुमेय सीमा 20 प्रतिशत (E20) तय है। मंत्री जैकब ने स्पष्ट किया कि यादृच्छिक (Random) रूप से एकत्र किए गए ईंधन के नमूनों को सरकारी प्रयोगशाला में परीक्षण के लिए भेजा जाएगा, जिसकी रिपोर्ट 10 दिनों के भीतर उपलब्ध होगी। 20 प्रतिशत से अधिक एथेनॉल बेचने वाले पेट्रोल पंपों को तुरंत सील कर दिया जाएगा और जिम्मेदार संस्थाओं के खिलाफ कानूनी कार्रवाई की जाएगी।

यह निरीक्षण कार्रवाई 2014 के एक राज्य नोटीफिकेशन के तहत की जा रही है, जो केंद्रीय मोटर स्पिरिट एंड हाई स्पीड डीजल (आपूर्ति और वितरण का नियमन और कदाचार निवारण) आदेश, 2005 के अंतर्गत जारी किया गया था। यह कानून नागरिक आपूर्ति और उपभोक्ता मामले आयुक्त से लेकर तालुक आपूर्ति अधिकारियों तक को जांच करने और कानूनी कार्रवाई शुरू करने का अधिकार देता है।

केरल में यह कार्रवाई कर्नाटक के खाद्य, नागरिक आपूर्ति और विधिक माप विज्ञान मंत्री रिजवान अरशद द्वारा लगाए गए आरोपों के बाद हुई है। अक्टूबर 2026 में कर्नाटक के सात जिलों—बेंगलुरु, कोलार, चिक्कबल्लापुरा, बेंगलुरु ग्रामीण, रामनगर, मंगलुरु और तुमकुरु—में लिए गए पेट्रोल के नमूनों में एथेनॉल की मात्रा 31.2 प्रतिशत तक पाए जाने का दावा किया गया था। हालांकि, सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र की तेल विपणन कंपनियों (OMCs) ने इन दावों को खारिज करते हुए कहा कि उनका E20 पेट्रोल भारतीय मानक ब्यूरो (BIS) के IS 17021 मापदंडों का पूरी तरह पालन करता है।

news.full_article_text:
### Uttarakhand Statehood Day Celebrations

Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended his heartfelt congratulations to the citizens of Uttarakhand on November 9, marking the state's Foundation Day. In his message, the Prime Minister recognized the contribution of the state's populace toward regional progress and highlighted Uttarakhand's cultural significance.

Uttarakhand was officially carved out of the northern Himalayan hill districts of Uttar Pradesh on November 9, 2000, under the Uttar Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000. It entered the Indian Union as the 27th state. Initially established under the name Uttaranchal, the state assembly passed legislation to formally rename it Uttarakhand in 2007, honoring the long-standing name used during the statehood movement.

hindi_translation.story_lead: प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने 9 नवंबर को उत्तराखंड के स्थापना दिवस के अवसर पर राज्य के नागरिकों को हार्दिक बधाई दी। उन्होंने राज्य की प्रगति यात्रा की सराहना की और इसकी निरंतर समृद्धि की कामना की।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### उत्तराखंड राज्य स्थापना दिवस समारोह

प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने 9 नवंबर को उत्तराखंड के स्थापना दिवस के अवसर पर राज्य की जनता को अपनी शुभकामनाएं दीं। अपने संदेश में प्रधानमंत्री ने क्षेत्रीय प्रगति में राज्य के निवासियों के योगदान को रेखांकित किया और उत्तराखंड के सांस्कृतिक महत्व को उजागर किया।

### राज्य गठन का ऐतिहासिक संदर्भ

उत्तराखंड को 9 नवंबर 2000 को उत्तर प्रदेश पुनर्गठन अधिनियम, 2000 के तहत उत्तर प्रदेश के उत्तरी पहाड़ी जिलों को अलग करके आधिकारिक तौर पर बनाया गया था। यह भारतीय संघ के 27वें राज्य के रूप में अस्तित्व में आया। प्रारंभ में 'उत्तरांचल' नाम से गठित इस राज्य का नाम 2007 में आधिकारिक रूप से बदलकर 'उत्तराखंड' कर दिया गया।

news.headline: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
news.story_lead: Footage shows derailed train carriages near Giza in Egypt - Published 8 November 2026, 15:06 GMT At least seven people have died in a train crash near the Egyptian city of Giza, with more than 100 injured. The country's railway authority said two trains travelling south from Giza and Cairo collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment. Images from the scene showed people looking inside overturned carriages for injured passengers as a massive emergency response was launched.
news.full_article_text: Footage shows derailed train carriages near Giza in Egypt - Published 8 November 2026, 15:06 GMT At least seven people have died in a train crash near the Egyptian city of Giza, with more than 100 injured. The country's railway authority said two trains travelling south from Giza and Cairo collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment. Images from the scene showed people looking inside overturned carriages for injured passengers as a massive emergency response was launched. Egyptian President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi said he had ordered state authorities to "investigate the circumstances of the accident, and hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent". The public prosecutor's office warned the death toll could rise. Uninjured passengers and bystanders searched derailed carriages for injured people The government said hospitals in the area had been put "on heightened alert" as they dealt with a massive influx of patients. Egypt's health minister Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said people were being treated for broken bones and head injuries. The Egyptian Red Crescent said it was providing aid and psychological support to victims and their families at the scene. The driver of one of the trains was among those who died in the crash, the ministry confirmed. The first train involved in the crash was travelling from Giza to Fayoum, south of Cairo, when it crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to Aswan, which was stationary on the tracks. Images from the scene showed some carriages had overturned, with the body of at least one appearing to have split in two. Trains between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended as cranes were dispatched to remove the wrecked trains. The railway authority has not said how long it expects this to take. The collision occurred in the area between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat, close to where Egypt's deadliest train tragedy occurred in February 2002, when a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor. In that incident, more than 370 people were officially reported killed, although some estimates put the toll considerably higher. Two further crashes in the area in 2009 killed dozens more. There were calls in Egypt on Sunday for the transport minister to resign over the latest deadly rail disaster. Foreign leaders and dignitaries have shared condolences and support for the victims. Saudi Arabia's ministry of foreign affairs expressed "solidarity" with Egypt and wished those hurt a speedy recovery. Turkey's ambassador to Egypt wrote on X that he extended "heartfelt condolences and sincere sympathy" to the victims, their families, and the Egyptian people. Related topics
